description:
DONE (s470bq, Opus, 2026-09-05).  Part B item B5, docs/generated-cl-ir-review.md
Â§3.3 (now marked CLOSED there).

A regex literal used to reach the runtime as ONE STRING carrying its perl
delimiters and its trailing flags -- `(p-regex "/pat/i")`, `(pcl::p-qr
"qr{p}gi")` -- so every consumer of the IR (this runtime included) had to
re-implement perl's delimiter/flag scan before it could see the pattern.  The
compiler ALREADY had the parts (PPI hands them over separately and
`_parse_regex_content` splits them); joining them back threw the structure away.

SHIPPED: all five entry points are MACROS over

  (p-regex            :pat "â¦" :flags "â¦" :tier T)
  (pcl::p-qr          :pat "â¦" :flags "â¦" :tier T)
  (pcl::p-regex-from-parts :pat FORM :flags "â¦" :tier :dynamic)
  (p-subst  :pat "â¦"|FORM :rep "â¦"|LAMBDA :flags "â¦" :tier T)
  (p-tr     :from "â¦" :to "â¦" :flags "â¦")            <- no :tier, not a regex

expanding to exactly the call the string form used to make, so the RUN is
byte-identical (the parse simply happens at the transpiler).  The OLD
positional form DIES at macroexpansion naming the form (rule 12): two shapes
reaching one entry point is exactly the mix a compatibility arm would hide, and
the generation bump makes the old shape unreachable anyway.

THE EMITTER SIDE IS ONE BUILDER.  `Pl::ExprToCL::_regex_literal_form` replaced
FOUR byte-identical arms (gen_leaf and gen_leaf_form each had an m// arm and a
qr// arm) -- which is precisely why the tier could not have been added in one
place before (rule 11).  `:pat` and `:flags` go out through
`_cl_string_literal_form`, the one string writer, so a pattern holding a
control character or an unrepresentable code point is escaped like any other
literal instead of being written raw (the #419 hole in regex literals, closed
by the routing rather than by a second escaper).

MEASURED: the s/// and tr/// modifier keywords are reproduced EXACTLY -- PPI
collapses `/xx` to a single `x` (probed), so `sort keys %$mods` is always
distinct single letters and the runtime's per-letter conversion gives the same
keyword list as the old `map { ":$_" }`.  The standing gap that `s///xx`
reaches the engine as `/x` is UNCHANGED, not fixed here.

Guard Pl/t/ir-data-form-01.t (the five keyword forms + one construct per tier);
the stale shape expectations in clform-01.t / regexp-subst-01.t / codegen-01.t
were repaired in the same commit (the s416 rule).
subject: Structured regex literals: p-regex / p-qr / p-regex-from-parts / p-subst / p-tr take a KEYWORD form and the old positional one dies at macroexpansion (flag-day, gen v2-800)
